I love, love, love this game- have loved it since release and will continue to love it for as long as I breathe. I never hesitate to purchase a new copy when I adopt a new gaming platform- when I was thru-hiking on the Appalachian Trail I would play this offline in hostels and in town stops on my phone, and fear I will never tire of it.

Despite having sunk (across varying platforms, what I assume to be) 1500+ hours into this masterpiece, I have not yet reached perfection- I am in no rush at all, and am a little sad that I am nearly there now- however, with the new update coming later this year, I have no worries or hesitations at all when it comes to beginning a new farm and starting the journey from the beginning once more. 

Absolutely recommend, my all-time favorite RPG, and I am always filled with so much joy and absolute enthusiasm when it comes to future updates. May be the perfec

I got this game about 10 years ago and I never really tried it properly until recently. It is actually a very very good game. I'm not usually into these kind of 'cosy' games but this one doesn't feel boring, or like I am doing nothing, there is a lot of gameplay and a lot to do. There is nothing I can add that others haven't already said over so many years, but I would recommend this game to anyone.
Usually this is great for relaxation, chilling, and building/growing on your farm... except the evil lying within the cave. I'd say this is a great recommendation alongside Fields of Mistria.

Wholesome game. It has a power of totally captivating you by the simpliest of tasks and routines. Yes, the game about farming (even though its a video game only) can be a bit exhausting at times, as you feel the urge to be as productive as possible, days seem short, time runs too fast, and there is still so mush left to do! The little farmer has no days off and works hard from 6 o'clock in the morning till 2AM, but he doesn't want no days off! And boy it is extremely satisfying to reap all the fruits of your hard labour. I love this game.

It's Stardew. Of course I'm gonna recommend it.


P.s. check out Haunted Choclatier in 2030!

Before anything else, a little context for the playtime shown above. At the time of writing I have just under three hours recorded on this PC version of Stardew Valley, but this isn't my first time on the farm. I originally played on Xbox around the time the game was released and put well over 200 hours into it there.

For some reason that I genuinely can't remember, I never actually finished that original journey.

So, many years later, I'm starting again.

And within minutes of arriving back in Stardew Valley, I remembered exactly why I spent so much time here in the first place.

🌱 What I love most about Stardew Valley is that it lets me play Stardew Valley.

Absolutely amazing game. Before you judge it and assume you won't like a farming game, it not only has farming, it has combat, mining, foraging, advancement, new areas, relationships, and lore.

Stardew Valley isn't just a game; it’s an absolute masterpiece and the ultimate escape (can be dangerous for those without restraint) . What creator ConcernedApe built single-handedly is nothing short of magic. 

From its insanely addictive farming-and-building loop to its charming townspeople (Maru for the win!), timeless pixel art, and breathtaking seasonal soundtrack, every single second spent in Pelican Town feels like a warm embrace. Whether you’re meticulously optimizing a massive farm or just spending a rainy day fishing by the river, the game respects your time and fills you with a genuine sense of peace and accomplishment.

It is cozy, rewarding, infinitely replayable, and quite simply one of the greatest video games ever made.

Score: 10/10 — Pure perfection.

A beautiful game that makes me discover new fun elements of it everytime I play it, I thought it was overhyped at first but then I saw how much I loved exploring the small world Concerned ape has put together for us

Honestly, it can be a dull and slow game.

However, it's excellent for gamers who are learning the ropes and for people who enjoy either the thrill of managing a simple farm or exploring how relationships develop in the idealized Stardew Valley. Fishing and mining, as mechanics, get old quick, nonetheless this may be exactly what some need in order to develop an appreciation for conservative lifestyles, nature, and the environment. Overall, it provides a relaxing experience with little to tell... and multiplayer offers an arguably more impactful experience, if played with the right friends.

Lastly, the game highlights the values of inclusion and inherent respect. For this reason, I cannot recommend the game; its heart belongs to the world, and it makes itself an abomination to my Lord.
